::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 30. 1865  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS. 55384 (1):  P. 319
:::

Dear Miss Yonge	

[Mr Sutcliffe](people/person_1933.qmd) is a very old friend of ours. [I](people/person_939.qmd) must write him on the subject of plain hand. He[,] the head of an Educational department[,] ought to know better.[^1]

I have sent you four copies of [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd) through [Nutt & Wells](organizations/other_178.qmd). I suppose you can get them thence.

[My sister](people/person_941.qmd) threatens you with a letter.[^1] But we wanted to see the first [chapter](organizations/other_177.qmd) in type first. The printer is doing this.

Yours ever truly
A. Macmillan

---

[^1]: CMY had misread Sutcliffe's name as Ratcliffe because of his poor handwriting.

**Note:** It seems that Macmillan’s sister-in-law, Frances Eliza Macmillan, was going to take a hand in the editing of 'Bethlehem'. She had suggested the Golden Deeds project, and perhaps 'Bethlehem' was also her idea.
